title: finding(console): the `user:profile` parity waiver still reads 「EMPTY SPEC SHAPE … PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS placeholder」 — both halves were falsified, by spec 17.3.0's retirement and by objectui#7122
body:
Path: none | 豁免理由已陈旧,无人能再评估 | 纯文档措辞

Filed by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat (PM session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) while closing objectui#7135, as the carrier for the one reading that card's delivery left behind. ⛔ Not graded here — an execution seat does not grade or route.

## The measurement

`apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts:674`-`:675`, read on objectui `origin/main` `030a675b0` at 2026-09-19T18:34Z:

```
'user:profile':
  'EMPTY SPEC SHAPE. Declared by the spec with no top-level key; in this repo it
   exists only as a `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` placeholder name, which is a scaffold
   rather than a renderer and publishes no authoring surface. objectui#8176.',
```

⭐ **Both halves of that waiver reason are now false**, and each was falsified by a different landed change:

| half of the stated reason | what it says | what is true today | falsified by |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 「Declared by the spec with no top-level key」 | the spec DECLARES it, with an empty shape | ⛔ the spec **no longer declares it at all** — it is RETIRED | `@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0, ruling B on objectstack#14159 (PR objectstack#15112, merged `97a22639`) |
| 「exists only as a `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` placeholder name」 | the repo still carries the placeholder | ⛔ objectui#7122 **took it out of `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS`** | objectui#7122 |

Readings behind the right-hand column, all taken at 2026-09-19T18:34Z:

- The **published, installed** package — `pnpm-lock.yaml` on `origin/main` resolves `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` (control: the whole `@objectstack/*` family resolves 17.4.0, one version, no split). In that tarball's own source, `src/ui/component.zod.ts:3000` reads `'user:profile': retiredComponentProps('user:profile')`, and `src/ui/page.zod.ts:85` exports `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES`.
- `packages/components/src/renderers/placeholders.tsx:88` states the removal in the first person: 「`'user:profile'` intentionally omitted … Retired across all three sites at once (objectui#7122): here, the Studio palette ledger (`app-shell` `previews/block-types.ts`), and the regenerated `@object-ui/cli` `known-schema-types.ts`」.

## ⭐ The part that makes this worth a card rather than a one-line edit

`element:form` left `PageComponentType` in **the same** 17.3.0 retirement — `placeholders.tsx:90` measures the lost set as exactly `['user:profile', 'element:form']`, gained set empty. Its waiver entry in the same file (`:667`) gives a **different** reason: 「NOT REGISTERED, DELIBERATELY … no renderer, use the object-bound `object-form` block」.

⇒ Two keys retired by one upstream change carry two unrelated waiver reasons, and **neither reason mentions the retirement**. So the question this card asks is not "fix a sentence", it is:

> **Is the waiver population derived from the spec enum at all?** If it is, a key the spec no longer declares should not need a waiver — it should have left the population. If it is not, then the list is a hand-maintained one whose entries can outlive their reasons, which is what both of these did.

⛔ This card does **not** assert which answer is right; that is a reading of `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`'s own population logic, not a guess to be made from the entries.

## ⚠️ Why this is not urgent, stated plainly

Nothing user-reachable is broken. The user-visible half of objectui#7135 — an authored page carrying `user:profile` drawing a red unknown-type panel — was fixed by objectui#7122 and by the upstream retirement. What is left is a **waiver whose stated reason is false**, which matters because a waiver is exactly the thing that is supposed to be read before a gap is dismissed.
